key_insight: A forked PINN with a separate control branch resolves gradient conflicts in non-Markovian open quantum systems, enabling joint simulation and control to train reliably.
engineering_relevance: This offers a unified, differentiable framework for designing quantum control pulses while accurately modeling dissipative dynamics in practical experimental settings.
method: Split simulation and control into separate branches
Use selective gradient flow to decouple conflicting objectives
Train on coupled open-quantum-dynamics equations with end-to-end differentiability
evidence_signal: On a two-qubit Heisenberg XXX model, the method reproduces non-Markovian features and achieves higher state-preparation fidelity than gradient ascent pulse engineering, chopped random basis, and standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on careful branch design and could be sensitive to how strongly the environment dissipates or approaches Markovian behavior.
paper_title: Forked Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Non-Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics and Control
